[34mInvestigated:[0m Inspected the compound implementation in src/index.ts (fmtCompound and format), the Options JSDoc, the README usage examples, and the compound test blocks in src/format.test.ts. Confirmed parse('1h 30m') returns NaN. Checked git status and the commit history on the branch.

[33mLearned:[0m Compound output truncates to whole seconds, drops leftover milliseconds, skips zero parts, uses days as the largest unit with no week, month, or year rollup, and prefixes negatives with '-'. It returns '0s' when all parts are zero. compound takes precedence over long. Compound output does not round-trip through parse(), which returns NaN for strings like '1h 30m'.

[32mCompleted:[0m The README has a "Compound Time Format" section with examples and rules; the earlier one-line example was moved into it. The Options JSDoc documents the compound option. format.test.ts gained rollover tests at each unit boundary, zero and negative multi-unit cases, and a check that compound: false or an omitted option leaves output unchanged. Jest reports 182 passing tests, up from 178, and biome check is clean. The feature commit is a35ee29; the whitespace fix is e3b0ddd on the same branch. The README and test changes are not yet committed.

[35mNext Steps:[0m Commit the uncommitted README and format.test.ts changes so the compound work is ready for review. Resolve whether the user wants the ParseDuration-compatible compound format (no spaces, hours as the largest unit, e.g. 1d 1h 30m becomes 25h30m). That would change the implementation, tests, and README, and the current format is unchanged until the user decides.

[36mNotes:[0m The whitespace fix e3b0ddd is stacked on the compound-format branch rather than main, so it is not yet isolated from the feature work. The README states that compound output is for display only and cannot be parsed back, which is the main trade-off to surface in review. No test covers the round-trip limitation; the README is the only place it is documented.
